input.question: Why do people think that there are an infinite number of universes?
input.ground_truth: Depends how you define universe. Theres the observable universe which is finite. We can only see so far out past earth. Most people believe space is infinite. If it wasnt, then what would exist after space? Anyway, if space is infinite and our observable universe is finite, then it is highly likely that other universes exist, and that there are an unlimited amount of them. If you define the universe as literally everything. Then there is only 1. And it is infinite. Any variations of it would just be contained in itself.

Question: Why do people think that there are an infinite number of universes?

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you have a big, big, *super* big box of marbles. In that box, there are so many marbles that you can never count them all, and for every marble, there could be a whole new box just like it, but maybe a little bit different inside.

Some smart people think that our universe is like one of those marbles, and maybe there are so many universes—so many that we can’t even count them—that it’s like there are an infinite number. They think this because when they look at how the universe works, it seems like it could keep going and making new places, just like how you could keep putting more and more marbles in the box forever and ever.

So, they guess that there might be an infinite number of universes, just like there could be an infinite number of marbles in a never-ending box. But it’s just a guess, because we can’t see all those other universes yet!
